hypothesis: moving the RAM RAF command behind InstructionClaim would remove queue interference from the InstructionClaim first-message join

falsification.pre_registered_kill_condition: reject if the InstructionClaim join saves less than 10 ms or remains above 25 ms
falsification.result: the intended order was observed, but InstructionClaim became slower

analysis.conclusion: RAM RAF submission order is not the cause of the exposed InstructionClaim wait
analysis.likely_boundary: InstructionClaim command scheduling before GPUStart or after GPUEnd, outside the measured GPU-active interval
analysis.code_action: revert the scheduling change and preserve the original RAM RAF overlap

next_experiment.design: clock-correlate InstructionClaim commit, scheduled, GPUStart, GPUEnd, and completion in same-binary isolated and production-queue controls
requirements: attribute the current 31.508500 ms join interval not covered by GPU-active time
show at least 10 ms of reducible pre-start or post-end delay before changing scheduling
leave RAM RAF completed before its first join
